writtenQuestions.q:
A camera films the motion of a swing in a park.

Let x(t) be the horizontal distance, in metres, from the camera to the seat of the swing at t seconds.

The seat is released from rest at a horizontal distance of 11.2 m from the camera.(a) The rate of change of x can be modelled by the equation dx/dt = −1.5π sin(5πt/4).

Find an expression for x(t). (2 marks)

(b) How many times does the swing reach the closest point to the camera during the first 10 seconds? (2 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) x(t) = ∫ −1.5π sin(5πt/4) dt
= −1.5π × [−cos(5πt/4)] ÷ (5π/4) + C
= (1.5π × 4)/(5π) × cos(5πt/4) + C
= 1.2 cos(5πt/4) + C.

Released from rest at 11.2 m means x(0) = 11.2:
1.2 cos 0 + C = 11.2, so 1.2 + C = 11.2 and C = 10.
x(t) = 1.2 cos(5πt/4) + 10.

(b) The closest point to the camera is the minimum of x, where cos(5πt/4) = −1, that is 5πt/4 = π, 3π, 5π, …
t = 0.8, 2.4, 4.0, 5.6, 7.2, 8.8, 10.4, … (one every full period of 2π ÷ (5π/4) = 1.6 seconds)

Within the first 10 seconds: t = 0.8, 2.4, 4.0, 5.6, 7.2, 8.8 — 6 times.

bandDescriptors.full: x(t) = 1.2 cos(5πt/4) + 10, then 6 times in the first 10 seconds.
bandDescriptors.partial: The integration is correct but the constant is not found from x(0) = 11.2, or the count in (b) is out by one — t = 10.4 lies outside the 10 seconds.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Antidifferentiate sin(kt) to −cos(kt)/k. Then the closest approach is the minimum of x, once per period, and the period is 2π ÷ (5π/4) = 1.6 seconds.

writtenQuestions.q:
The graph of y = f(x), where f(x) = a|x − b| + c, passes through the points (3, −5), (6, 7) and (9, −5) as shown in the diagram.(a) Find the values of a, b and c. (3 marks)

(b) The line y = mx cuts the graph of y = f(x) in two distinct places.

Find all possible values of m. (2 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) The graph is symmetric about its vertex, which the diagram shows at (6, 7). For y = a|x − b| + c the vertex is (b, c), so b = 6 and c = 7.
Substitute (3, −5):
a|3 − 6| + 7 = −5
3a = −12, so a = −4.
a = −4, b = 6, c = 7.

(b) f(x) = −4|x − 6| + 7 has two straight branches:
left branch (x < 6): y = 4x − 17
right branch (x ≥ 6): y = −4x + 31

The line y = mx passes through the origin. It meets the right branch where mx = −4x + 31, that is x = 31/(m + 4), and that intersection lies on the branch (x ≥ 6) only when −4 < m ≤ 7/6.
It meets the left branch where mx = 4x − 17, that is x = 17/(4 − m), and that lies on the branch (x < 6) only when m < 7/6 or m > 4.

Both branches are cut, in distinct points, exactly when
−4 < m < 7/6.

(At m = 7/6 the line passes through the vertex (6, 7) and touches at a single point; at m = −4 the line is parallel to the right branch.)

bandDescriptors.full: a = −4, b = 6, c = 7 in (a), and −4 < m < 7/6 in (b), with both endpoints correctly excluded.
bandDescriptors.partial: (a) fully correct but (b) gives only one boundary, or includes an endpoint — at m = 7/6 the line passes through the vertex and meets the graph once, and at m = −4 it is parallel to a branch.
bandDescriptors.minimal: The vertex of y = a|x − b| + c is (b, c), which the diagram gives directly. For (b), write the two branches as separate straight lines and ask when y = mx meets each one on its own side of x = 6.

writtenQuestions.q:
The curve y = f(x) is shown on the diagram. The equation of the tangent to the curve at point T(−1, 6) is y = x + 7. At a point R, another tangent parallel to the tangent at T is drawn.The gradient function of the curve is given by dy/dx = 3x² − 6x − 8.

Find the coordinates of R.
writtenQuestions.answer:
The tangent at T has gradient 1, so at R the gradient is also 1:
3x² − 6x − 8 = 1
3x² − 6x − 9 = 0
x² − 2x − 3 = 0
(x − 3)(x + 1) = 0, so x = 3 or x = −1.
x = −1 is the point T, so R has x = 3.

To find the y-value, antidifferentiate:
y = x³ − 3x² − 8x + C
T(−1, 6) lies on the curve: −1 − 3 + 8 + C = 6, so C = 2.
y = x³ − 3x² − 8x + 2

At x = 3: y = 27 − 27 − 24 + 2 = −22.

R = (3, −22).

bandDescriptors.full: R = (3, −22) — x = 3 from equating the gradient function to 1, and y from antidifferentiating and using T(−1, 6) to find the constant.
bandDescriptors.partial: x = 3 found but the y-value is wrong, usually because the constant of integration was omitted or found from the tangent rather than the curve.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Parallel tangents have equal gradients, and the tangent at T is y = x + 7, so its gradient is 1. Set the gradient function equal to 1 for the x-value, then antidifferentiate and use T to fix + C.

writtenQuestions.q:
A continuous random variable X has probability density function f(x) given by
{12x²(1 − x),   for 0 ≤ x ≤ 1
0,   for all other values of x


(a) Find the mode of X. (2 marks)

(b) Find the cumulative distribution function for the given probability density function. (2 marks)

(c) Without calculating the median, show that the mode is greater than the median. (2 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) The mode is where f is greatest. Expand: f(x) = 12x² − 12x³.
f′(x) = 24x − 36x² = 12x(2 − 3x)
f′(x) = 0 at x = 0 and x = 2/3. Since f′ changes from positive to negative at x = 2/3, that is the maximum.
Mode = 2/3.

(b) For 0 ≤ x ≤ 1,
F(x) = ∫₀ˣ (12t² − 12t³) dt = [4t³ − 3t⁴]₀ˣ = 4x³ − 3x⁴.
So F(x) = 0 for x < 0, F(x) = 4x³ − 3x⁴ for 0 ≤ x ≤ 1, and F(x) = 1 for x > 1.
(Check: F(1) = 4 − 3 = 1.)

(c) Evaluate F at the mode:
F(2/3) = 4(8/27) − 3(16/81) = 32/27 − 16/27 = 16/27 ≈ 0.593.
That is more than 0.5, so more than half the probability lies below x = 2/3. F is increasing, so the median — the value where F = 0.5 — must lie to the left of 2/3.
Therefore the mode is greater than the median.

bandDescriptors.full: Mode 2/3, F(x) = 4x³ − 3x⁴ on [0, 1], and F(2/3) = 16/27 > 0.5 used to place the median below the mode.
bandDescriptors.partial: Mode and cumulative distribution function correct, but (c) attempts to solve for the median instead of comparing F(2/3) with 0.5.
bandDescriptors.minimal: The mode maximises f, so solve f′(x) = 0. The cumulative distribution function is ∫₀ˣ f(t) dt. For (c), the median is where F = 0.5 — so just work out F at the mode and compare.

writtenQuestions.q:
Let f(x) = e−x sin x.

(a) Find the coordinates of the stationary points of f(x) for 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π. You do NOT need to check the nature of the stationary points. (3 marks)

Part (b), which asked for the graph of y = f(x) to be sketched on a printed set of axes showing stationary points and intercepts, is not included here.
writtenQuestions.answer:
Differentiate with the product rule:
f′(x) = −e⁻ˣ sin x + e⁻ˣ cos x
= e⁻ˣ(cos x − sin x).

e⁻ˣ is never zero, so f′(x) = 0 when cos x = sin x, that is tan x = 1.
For 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π: x = π/4 and x = 5π/4.

f(π/4) = e^(−π/4) × √2/2 ≈ 0.322
f(5π/4) = e^(−5π/4) × (−√2/2) ≈ −0.014

Stationary points: (π/4, (√2/2)e^(−π/4)) ≈ (0.785, 0.322) and (5π/4, −(√2/2)e^(−5π/4)) ≈ (3.927, −0.014).

bandDescriptors.full: Both stationary points, x = π/4 and x = 5π/4, with their y-coordinates.
bandDescriptors.partial: The derivative and tan x = 1 are correct but only one solution is given in the domain, or the y-coordinates are not found.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Use the product rule, then factor out e⁻ˣ — it is never zero, so the stationary points come from cos x = sin x alone. Look for every solution of tan x = 1 between 0 and 2π.

omittedParts.reason: The student must sketch y = e⁻ˣ sin x on printed axes for 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π, showing the stationary points and intercepts. The engine cannot accept or mark a hand-drawn graph.

writtenQuestions.q:
Four Year 12 students want to organise a graduation party. All four students have the same probability, P(F), of being available next Friday. All four students have the same probability, P(S), of being available next Saturday.

It is given that P(F) = 3/10, P(S|F) = 1/3, and P(F|S) = 1/8.

Kim is one of the four students.

(a) Is Kim’s availability next Friday independent from his availability next Saturday? Justify your answer. (1 mark)

(b) Show that the probability that Kim is available next Saturday is 4/5. (2 marks)

(c) What is the probability that at least one of the four students is NOT available next Saturday? (2 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) No. If F and S were independent then P(S|F) would equal P(S). Here P(S|F) = 1/3, while P(S) = 4/5 (found in part (b)), and 1/3 ≠ 4/5, so the two events are not independent.

(b) P(F ∩ S) = P(S|F) × P(F) = (1/3)(3/10) = 1/10.
P(F|S) = P(F ∩ S)/P(S), so
1/8 = (1/10)/P(S)
P(S) = (1/10) × 8 = 8/10 = 4/5.

(c) P(a given student is available on Saturday) = 4/5, and the four students are independent of one another.
P(at least one NOT available) = 1 − P(all four available)
= 1 − (4/5)⁴
= 1 − 256/625
= 369/625
= 0.5904.

bandDescriptors.full: Not independent because P(S|F) ≠ P(S); P(S) = 4/5 shown from P(F ∩ S) = 1/10; and P(at least one not available) = 1 − (4/5)⁴ = 369/625.
bandDescriptors.partial: (b) correct but (c) computes P(all four unavailable) as (1/5)⁴ instead of using the complement of 'all four available'.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Start with P(F ∩ S) = P(S|F)P(F). That single value unlocks P(S) through the definition of P(F|S). For (c), 'at least one' almost always means 1 minus the probability of none.

writtenQuestions.q:
The curves y = e−2x and y = e−x − 1/4 intersect at exactly one point as shown in the diagram. The point of intersection has coordinates (ln 2, 1/4). (Do NOT prove this.)(a) Show that the area bounded by the two curves and the y-axis, as shaded in the diagram, is (1/4)ln 2 − 1/8. (3 marks)

(b) Find the values of k such that the curves y = e−2x and y = e−x + k intersect at two points. (3 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) Between x = 0 and x = ln 2 the upper curve is y = e⁻²ˣ and the lower is y = e⁻ˣ − 1/4.
Area = ∫₀^(ln 2) [e⁻²ˣ − e⁻ˣ + 1/4] dx
= [−½e⁻²ˣ + e⁻ˣ + x/4]₀^(ln 2)

At x = ln 2: e⁻ˣ = 1/2 and e⁻²ˣ = 1/4, giving
−½(1/4) + 1/2 + (ln 2)/4 = 3/8 + (ln 2)/4
At x = 0: −½ + 1 + 0 = 1/2

Area = 3/8 + (ln 2)/4 − 1/2 = (1/4)ln 2 − 1/8.

(b) Set the curves equal: e⁻²ˣ = e⁻ˣ + k.
Let u = e⁻ˣ, so u > 0, and every positive u corresponds to exactly one value of x.
u² = u + k
u² − u − k = 0

Two intersections means two distinct positive roots u.
Discriminant: 1 + 4k > 0, so k > −1/4.
Product of roots = −k > 0, so k < 0.
Sum of roots = 1 > 0, consistent.

So −1/4 < k < 0.

bandDescriptors.full: The area established as (1/4)ln 2 − 1/8, and −1/4 < k < 0 in (b) from requiring two distinct positive roots of u² − u − k = 0.
bandDescriptors.partial: (a) correct but (b) only applies the discriminant, giving k > −1/4 and missing the requirement that both roots be positive.
bandDescriptors.minimal: In (a) integrate (upper − lower) from 0 to ln 2. In (b) substitute u = e⁻ˣ to get a quadratic, and remember u must be positive for a real x to exist — the discriminant alone is not enough.

writtenQuestions.q:
The table shows the types of customer complaints received by an online business in a month.
Type of complaintFrequencyCumulative frequencyCumulative percentage
Stock shortage989849
Delivery fee62A80
Delivery time2418492
Damaged item8192B
Returns policy619899
Product information2200100
Total200

(a) What are the values of A and B? (2 marks)

(b) The data from the table are shown in the following Pareto chart.The manager will address 80% of the complaints.

Which types of complaints will the manager address? (1 mark)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) A is the cumulative frequency after Delivery fee:
A = 98 + 62 = 160.

B is the cumulative percentage after Damaged item:
B = 192/200 × 100 = 96.

(b) Reading the cumulative percentage line, Stock shortage alone reaches 49% and Stock shortage together with Delivery fee reaches 80%.

So the manager will address Stock shortage and Delivery fee.

bandDescriptors.full: A = 160 and B = 96, and the two complaint types identified are Stock shortage and Delivery fee.
bandDescriptors.partial: One of A or B correct, or the right idea in (b) but only one complaint type named. B is a percentage of the 200 total, not a frequency.

writtenQuestions.q:
A student believes that the time it takes for an ice cube to melt (M minutes) varies inversely with the room temperature (T°C). The student observes that at a room temperature of 15°C it takes 12 minutes for an ice cube to melt.

(a) Find the equation relating M and T. (2 marks)

Part (b), which asked for a table of values to be completed and the relationship graphed on a printed grid from T = 5°C to T = 30°C, is not included here.
writtenQuestions.answer:
Inverse variation means M = k/T for some constant k.

Substitute the observation M = 12 when T = 15:
12 = k/15
k = 180.

So M = 180/T.

bandDescriptors.full: M = 180/T, with the constant found by substituting M = 12 and T = 15 into M = k/T.
bandDescriptors.partial: The form M = k/T is set up correctly but k is not found, or the relationship is written as direct variation M = kT.
bandDescriptors.minimal: “Varies inversely” means M = k/T, not M = kT. Substitute the single given pair of values to find k.

omittedParts.reason: The student must complete a printed table of values and then draw the graph of the relationship on a printed grid. The engine cannot accept or mark a hand-drawn graph.

writtenQuestions.q: Use two applications of the trapezoidal rule to find an approximate value of ∫₀² √(1 + x²) dx. Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.

bandDescriptors.partial: The rule is applied correctly but the middle ordinate is not doubled, or the answer is not rounded to 2 decimal places.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Two applications of the trapezoidal rule use three ordinates, so h = (2 − 0)/2 = 1. The interior ordinate is counted twice.

writtenQuestions.q: The graph of y = k sin(ax) is shown.What are the values of k and a?
writtenQuestions.answer:
Amplitude: the curve runs between y = 4 and y = −4, so k = 4.

Period: the curve rises through zero at x = 0 and again at x = 6π, so the period is 6π.

For y = k sin(ax) the period is 2π/a, so
2π/a = 6π
a = 1/3.

k = 4 and a = 1/3, giving y = 4 sin(x/3).

bandDescriptors.full: k = 4 and a = 1/3, with the amplitude read from the maximum and a found from the period 6π.
bandDescriptors.partial: The amplitude is correct but a is wrong — a common slip is reading the period as 3π (the gap between consecutive zeros) rather than 6π (the gap between consecutive rising zeros).
bandDescriptors.minimal: Amplitude is the maximum height. The period of sin(ax) is 2π/a, and one full period runs from one upward crossing of the axis to the next.

writtenQuestions.q:
In a bag there are 3 six-sided dice. Two of the dice have faces marked 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. The other is a special die with faces marked 1, 2, 3, 5, 5, 5.

One die is randomly selected and tossed.

(a) What is the probability that the die shows a 5? (1 mark)

(b) Given that the die shows a 5, what is the probability that it is the special die? (1 mark)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) P(ordinary die) = 2/3 and that die shows a 5 with probability 1/6.
P(special die) = 1/3 and that die shows a 5 with probability 3/6 = 1/2.

P(5) = (2/3)(1/6) + (1/3)(1/2)
= 2/18 + 3/18
= 5/18.

(b) P(special | 5) = P(special and 5) ÷ P(5)
= (3/18) ÷ (5/18)
= 3/5.

bandDescriptors.full: P(5) = 5/18 and P(special | 5) = 3/5.
bandDescriptors.partial: One part correct. A common slip in (a) is forgetting that two of the three dice are ordinary, so the ordinary branch carries weight 2/3, not 1/2.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Weight each die by the chance of selecting it: 2/3 for an ordinary die, 1/3 for the special one. Then (b) is P(special and 5) divided by the P(5) from (a).

writtenQuestions.q: The parabola y = x² meets the line y = 2x + 3 at the points (−1, 1) and (3, 9) as shown in the diagram.Find the area enclosed by the parabola and the line.
writtenQuestions.answer:
Between x = −1 and x = 3 the line lies above the parabola, so

Area = ∫₋₁³ [(2x + 3) − x²] dx
= [x² + 3x − x³/3]₋₁³

At x = 3: 9 + 9 − 9 = 9.
At x = −1: 1 − 3 + 1/3 = −5/3.

Area = 9 − (−5/3) = 32/3 square units (≈ 10.67 square units).

bandDescriptors.full: 32/3 square units, from ∫₋₁³ (2x + 3 − x²) dx.
bandDescriptors.partial: The integrand or the limits are right but an arithmetic slip follows — most often mishandling the negative lower limit, where x³/3 becomes +1/3.
bandDescriptors.minimal: The area between two curves is ∫ (upper − lower) dx between the points of intersection. Here the line is the upper curve on −1 ≤ x ≤ 3.

writtenQuestions.q:
Cards are stacked to build a ‘house of cards’. A house of cards with 3 rows is shown.

A house of cards requires 3 cards in the top row, 6 cards in the next row, and each successive row has 3 more cards than the previous row.(a) Show that a house of cards with 12 rows has a total of 234 cards. (2 marks)

(b) Another house of cards has a total of 828 cards.

How many rows are in this house of cards? (3 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
The rows form an arithmetic series with first term a = 3 and common difference d = 3.

(a) Sn = (n/2)[2a + (n − 1)d] = (n/2)[6 + 3(n − 1)] = 3n(n + 1)/2.

For n = 12: S₁₂ = 3 × 12 × 13 ÷ 2 = 468/2 = 234 cards, as required.

(b) Set 3n(n + 1)/2 = 828:
n(n + 1) = 552
n² + n − 552 = 0

n = (−1 + √(1 + 2208))/2 = (−1 + √2209)/2 = (−1 + 47)/2 = 23.
(The negative root is rejected.)

The house of cards has 23 rows.

bandDescriptors.full: (a) The arithmetic sum 3n(n + 1)/2 is derived and evaluated at n = 12 to give 234. (b) Solving 3n(n + 1)/2 = 828 gives n = 23 rows.
bandDescriptors.partial: Part (a) shown but the quadratic in (b) is not solved, or both roots are kept when only the positive one makes sense.
bandDescriptors.minimal: The row sizes 3, 6, 9, … form an arithmetic series with a = 3 and d = 3. Use Sn = (n/2)[2a + (n − 1)d], then set that sum equal to 828 and solve for n.

writtenQuestions.q:
(a) Differentiate y = (x² + 1)⁴. (2 marks)

(b) Hence, or otherwise, find ∫ x(x² + 1)³ dx. (1 mark)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) Chain rule with u = x² + 1, so du/dx = 2x:
dy/dx = 4(x² + 1)³ × 2x
= 8x(x² + 1)³.

(b) Part (a) says the derivative of (x² + 1)⁴ is 8x(x² + 1)³, so
∫ 8x(x² + 1)³ dx = (x² + 1)⁴ + C.

Dividing by 8:
∫ x(x² + 1)³ dx = (1/8)(x² + 1)⁴ + C.

bandDescriptors.full: dy/dx = 8x(x² + 1)³ and ∫ x(x² + 1)³ dx = (1/8)(x² + 1)⁴ + C.
bandDescriptors.partial: The derivative is correct but the factor of 1/8 is dropped in (b), or the chain-rule factor 2x is omitted in (a).
bandDescriptors.minimal: Differentiate with the chain rule, then read (b) backwards from (a): the integrand is your derivative divided by 8, so the integral is (x² + 1)⁴ divided by 8.

writtenQuestions.q:
The graph of the function f(x) = x² is translated m units to the right, dilated vertically by a scale factor of k and then translated 5 units down. The equation of the transformed function is g(x) = 3x² − 12x + 7.

Find the values of m and k.
writtenQuestions.answer:
Apply the transformations in order:
translate m right:  (x − m)²
dilate vertically by k:  k(x − m)²
translate 5 down:  k(x − m)² − 5.

So g(x) = k(x − m)² − 5 = kx² − 2kmx + km² − 5.

Compare with 3x² − 12x + 7:
x² term: k = 3
x term: −2km = −12, so −6m = −12 and m = 2.

Check the constant: km² − 5 = 3(4) − 5 = 7 ✓

m = 2 and k = 3.

bandDescriptors.full: m = 2 and k = 3, obtained by writing g(x) = k(x − m)² − 5 and comparing coefficients (or by completing the square).
bandDescriptors.partial: k = 3 found from the x² coefficient but m not found, or the transformations applied in the wrong order so the −5 is dilated too.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Build the image step by step: x² → (x − m)² → k(x − m)² → k(x − m)² − 5. Then expand and match coefficients with 3x² − 12x + 7.

writtenQuestions.q:
A scientist is studying the growth of bacteria. The scientist models the number of bacteria, N, by the equation

N(t) = 200e0.013t,

where t is the number of hours after starting the experiment.

(a) What is the initial number of bacteria in the experiment? (1 mark)

(b) What is the number of bacteria 24 hours after starting the experiment? (1 mark)

(c) What is the rate of increase in the number of bacteria 24 hours after starting the experiment? (2 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) Initially t = 0, so N(0) = 200e⁰ = 200 bacteria.

(b) N(24) = 200e^(0.013 × 24) = 200e^0.312 ≈ 200 × 1.36615 ≈ 273.23,
so about 273 bacteria.

(c) The rate of increase is N′(t):
N′(t) = 200 × 0.013 × e^(0.013t) = 2.6e^(0.013t).

N′(24) = 2.6e^0.312 ≈ 2.6 × 1.36615 ≈ 3.55,
so the number of bacteria is increasing at about 3.55 bacteria per hour.

bandDescriptors.full: 200 initially, about 273 after 24 hours, and a rate of about 3.55 bacteria per hour at t = 24.
bandDescriptors.partial: Parts (a) and (b) correct but (c) evaluates N(24) again instead of N′(24), or the chain-rule factor 0.013 is dropped when differentiating.
bandDescriptors.minimal: “Initial” means t = 0. A “rate of increase” is a derivative: differentiate N(t) = 200e^(0.013t) first, then substitute t = 24.

Option 1: Depositing a single amount of $40 000 today, earning interest of 1.2% per annum, compounded monthly.

Option 2: Depositing $1000 at the end of each quarter, earning interest of 2.4% per annum, compounded quarterly.

writtenQuestions.q: Find the global maximum and minimum values of y = x³ − 6x² + 8, where −1 ≤ x ≤ 7.
writtenQuestions.answer:
Differentiate: dy/dx = 3x² − 12x = 3x(x − 4).

Stationary points where dy/dx = 0: x = 0 and x = 4. Both lie in −1 ≤ x ≤ 7.

Evaluate y at the stationary points and at both endpoints:
y(−1) = −1 − 6 + 8 = 1
y(0)  = 8
y(4)  = 64 − 96 + 8 = −24
y(7)  = 343 − 294 + 8 = 57

Global maximum: y = 57 at x = 7.
Global minimum:  y = −24 at x = 4.

bandDescriptors.full: Global maximum 57 at x = 7 and global minimum −24 at x = 4, with the endpoints tested as well as the stationary points.
bandDescriptors.partial: The stationary points are found but the endpoints are not tested, so the local maximum y = 8 at x = 0 is offered as the global maximum instead of 57.
bandDescriptors.minimal: On a closed interval the global extremes occur either at a stationary point or at an endpoint. Find both stationary points, then compare y at x = −1, 0, 4 and 7.

writtenQuestions.q:
The depth of water in a bay rises and falls with the tide. On a particular day the depth of the water, d metres, can be modelled by the equation

d = 1.3 − 0.6 cos(4πt/25),

where t is the time in hours since low tide.

(a) Find the depth of water at low tide and at high tide. (2 marks)

(b) What is the time interval, in hours, between two successive low tides? (1 mark)

(c) For how long between successive low tides will the depth of water be at least 1 metre? (3 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) cos takes values from −1 to 1.
Low tide: cos(4πt/25) = 1, so d = 1.3 − 0.6 = 0.7 m.
High tide: cos(4πt/25) = −1, so d = 1.3 + 0.6 = 1.9 m.

(b) The period is 2π ÷ (4π/25) = 2π × 25/(4π) = 12.5 hours.

(c) Require d ≥ 1:
1.3 − 0.6 cos(4πt/25) ≥ 1
−0.6 cos(4πt/25) ≥ −0.3
cos(4πt/25) ≤ 0.5.

Let θ = 4πt/25. Over one period 0 ≤ θ ≤ 2π, cos θ ≤ 0.5 for π/3 ≤ θ ≤ 5π/3,
an interval of length 5π/3 − π/3 = 4π/3.

Since t = 25θ/(4π), the corresponding time is
(25/(4π)) × 4π/3 = 25/3 hours ≈ 8.33 hours (8 hours 20 minutes).

bandDescriptors.full: 0.7 m at low tide and 1.9 m at high tide, a 12.5 hour interval, and the depth is at least 1 m for 25/3 ≈ 8.33 hours.
bandDescriptors.partial: Parts (a) and (b) correct but (c) solves only for the first crossing rather than the whole interval, or the inequality sign is not reversed when dividing by −0.6.
bandDescriptors.minimal: The extremes come from cos = ±1. The period of cos(kt) is 2π/k. In (c), rearrange to cos(4πt/25) ≤ 0.5 — reversing the inequality when you divide by a negative — and find the whole range of angles that satisfy it.

writtenQuestions.q:
Jo is researching the relationship between the ages of teenage characters in television series and the ages of actors playing these characters.

After collecting the data, Jo finds that the correlation coefficient is 0.4564.

A scatterplot showing the data is drawn. The line of best fit with equation y = −7.51 + 1.85x, is also drawn.Describe and interpret the data and other information provided, with reference to the context given.
writtenQuestions.answer:
Form and direction: the scatterplot shows a positive, roughly linear association — older characters tend to be played by older actors.

Strength: r = 0.4564 is positive but only moderate, so the association is weak to moderate. The scatterplot supports this: at each character age the actors' ages are widely spread (for example, at 15 years the actors range from about 14 to 26), so the points do not cluster tightly about the line.

Gradient: 1.85 means that, on average, each extra year of character age is associated with about 1.85 extra years of actor age.

Intercept: −7.51 is the predicted actor age for a character aged 0. This has no meaning in context — it lies far outside the range of the data (character ages 14 to 17), so it is extrapolation.

Other features: nearly all the points lie above the line y = x, so actors are generally older than the characters they play — at a character age of 15 the line predicts about 20.3 years. The data cover only a narrow range of character ages, so predictions outside 14–17 years are unreliable, and the correlation shown does not establish that character age causes actor age.

bandDescriptors.full: Describes the positive, moderate, roughly linear association; interprets r = 0.4564, the gradient 1.85 and the intercept −7.51 in context; and notes that actors are generally older than their characters and that the narrow data range makes extrapolation unreliable.
bandDescriptors.partial: Describes the association and quotes the correlation coefficient, but does not interpret the gradient or the intercept in the context of ages, or treats the intercept −7.51 as if it were meaningful.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Comment on direction, form and strength of the association, then say what the gradient 1.85 and the intercept −7.51 mean for actors and characters — and whether the intercept makes sense given the character ages actually in the data.

writtenQuestions.q:
Let f(x) = sin(2x).

Find the value of x, for 0 < x < π, for which f′(x) = −√3 AND f″(x) = 2.
writtenQuestions.answer:
Differentiate twice:
f′(x) = 2 cos 2x
f″(x) = −4 sin 2x

First condition: 2 cos 2x = −√3, so cos 2x = −√3/2.
Second condition: −4 sin 2x = 2, so sin 2x = −1/2.

Both cos 2x and sin 2x are negative, so 2x lies in the third quadrant. The reference angle with cosine √3/2 and sine 1/2 is π/6, so
2x = π + π/6 = 7π/6.

Since 0 < x < π gives 0 < 2x < 2π, this is the only solution.

x = 7π/12.

bandDescriptors.full: x = 7π/12, from cos 2x = −√3/2 and sin 2x = −1/2 placing 2x = 7π/6.
bandDescriptors.partial: Both derivatives correct and one equation solved, but the two conditions are not combined — solving cos 2x = −√3/2 alone gives 2x = 5π/6 as well, which the sine condition rules out.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Differentiate twice, then use both conditions together. The signs of sin 2x and cos 2x fix which quadrant 2x is in; only then halve to get x.

writtenQuestions.q:
The life span of batteries from a particular factory is normally distributed with a mean of 840 hours and a standard deviation of 80 hours.

It is known from statistical tables that for this distribution approximately 60% of the batteries have a life span of less than 860 hours.

What is the approximate percentage of batteries with a life span between 820 and 920 hours?
writtenQuestions.answer:
Standardise each value with z = (x − μ)/σ, where μ = 840 and σ = 80.

860 → z = 20/80 = 0.25, and we are told P(Z < 0.25) ≈ 0.60.
820 → z = −20/80 = −0.25
920 → z = 80/80 = 1

By symmetry, P(Z < −0.25) = 1 − P(Z < 0.25) = 1 − 0.60 = 0.40.

From the empirical rule, 68% of values lie within one standard deviation, so
P(Z < 1) = 0.5 + 0.34 = 0.84.

P(820 < X < 920) = P(−0.25 < Z < 1)
= 0.84 − 0.40
= 0.44.

About 44% of the batteries.

bandDescriptors.partial: One of the two tail probabilities is found correctly. A common slip is taking P(Z < −0.25) as 0.60 rather than using symmetry to get 0.40.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Standardise all three values. The given 60% fixes P(Z < 0.25); symmetry then gives P(Z < −0.25). Use the empirical 68% rule for z = 1, then subtract.

writtenQuestions.q:
Let f(x) = xe−2x.

It is given that f′(x) = e−2x − 2xe−2x.

(a) Show that f″(x) = 4(x − 1)e−2x. (2 marks)

(b) Find any stationary points of f(x) and determine their nature. (2 marks)

Part (c), which asked for the curve y = xe−2x to be sketched showing stationary points, points of inflection and intercepts, is not included here.
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) Differentiate f′(x) = e⁻²ˣ − 2xe⁻²ˣ term by term.

d/dx (e⁻²ˣ) = −2e⁻²ˣ
d/dx (2xe⁻²ˣ) = 2e⁻²ˣ + 2x(−2e⁻²ˣ) = 2e⁻²ˣ − 4xe⁻²ˣ  (product rule)

So f″(x) = −2e⁻²ˣ − (2e⁻²ˣ − 4xe⁻²ˣ)
= −4e⁻²ˣ + 4xe⁻²ˣ
= 4(x − 1)e⁻²ˣ, as required.

(b) Stationary points where f′(x) = 0:
e⁻²ˣ(1 − 2x) = 0.
e⁻²ˣ is never zero, so 1 − 2x = 0 and x = 1/2.

y-value: f(1/2) = (1/2)e⁻¹ = 1/(2e) ≈ 0.184.

Nature: f″(1/2) = 4(1/2 − 1)e⁻¹ = −2e⁻¹ < 0, so the curve is concave down there.

There is a single stationary point, a maximum at (1/2, 1/(2e)).

bandDescriptors.full: f″(x) = 4(x − 1)e⁻²ˣ shown, and a maximum turning point at (1/2, 1/(2e)) confirmed by f″(1/2) < 0.
bandDescriptors.partial: The second derivative is shown but the stationary point's nature is not determined, or x = 1/2 is found without its y-coordinate.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Differentiate f′ using the product rule on the 2xe⁻²ˣ term. For (b), factor e⁻²ˣ out of f′ — it is never zero, so only 1 − 2x = 0 matters — then test the sign of f″ there.

omittedParts.reason: The student must sketch the curve y = xe⁻²ˣ, showing stationary points, points of inflection and intercepts with the axes. The engine cannot accept or mark a hand-drawn graph.

writtenQuestions.q:
The graph of the circle x² + y² = 2 is shown.

The interval connecting the origin, O, and the point (1, 1) makes an angle θ with the positive x-axis.(a) By considering the value of θ, find the exact area of the shaded region, as shown on the diagram. (2 marks)

Part of the hyperbola y = a/(b − x) − 1 which passes through the points (0, 0) and (1, 1) is drawn with the circle x² + y² = 2 as shown.(b) Show that a = b = 2. (2 marks)

(c) Using parts (a) and (b), find the exact area of the region bounded by the hyperbola, the positive x-axis and the circle as shown on the diagram. (3 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) The point (1, 1) gives tan θ = 1/1, so θ = π/4. The circle has radius √2, so r² = 2.

Sector Oxy from the positive x-axis round to (1, 1):
Area = ½r²θ = ½ × 2 × π/4 = π/4.

The shaded region is that sector with the triangle with vertices (0, 0), (1, 0) and (1, 1) removed:
Triangle area = ½ × 1 × 1 = ½.

Shaded area = π/4 − ½ square units.

(b) Through (0, 0):  0 = a/(b − 0) − 1, so a/b = 1 and a = b.
Through (1, 1):  1 = a/(b − 1) − 1, so a/(b − 1) = 2 and a = 2b − 2.

Substituting a = b:  b = 2b − 2, so b = 2 and hence a = 2, as required.

(c) With a = b = 2 the hyperbola is y = 2/(2 − x) − 1.

Area under the hyperbola from x = 0 to x = 1:
∫₀¹ [2/(2 − x) − 1] dx = [−2 ln(2 − x) − x]₀¹
= (−2 ln 1 − 1) − (−2 ln 2 − 0)
= 2 ln 2 − 1.

From x = 1 to x = √2 the region is bounded above by the circle, and that piece is exactly the shaded region from part (a): π/4 − ½.

Total area = (2 ln 2 − 1) + (π/4 − ½)
= 2 ln 2 + π/4 − 3/2 square units.

bandDescriptors.full: (a) π/4 − ½. (b) a = b = 2 shown from both given points. (c) 2 ln 2 + π/4 − 3/2 square units, built from the integral of the hyperbola plus the region from part (a).
bandDescriptors.partial: Parts (a) and (b) correct but (c) integrates the hyperbola only, missing the circular piece from x = 1 to x = √2, or forgets to subtract the triangle in (a).
bandDescriptors.minimal: In (a), θ = π/4 and r² = 2, so use ½r²θ for the sector and subtract the right-angled triangle. In (b), substitute both points to get two equations in a and b. In (c), split the region at x = 1 and reuse (a) for the right-hand piece.

writtenQuestions.q:
(a) The diagram shows the graph of y = 2−x. Also shown on the diagram are the first 5 of an infinite number of rectangular strips of width 1 unit and height y = 2−x for non-negative integer values of x. For example, the second rectangle shown has width 1 and height ½.The sum of the areas of the rectangles forms a geometric series.

Show that the limiting sum of this series is 2. (1 mark)

(b) Show that ∫₀⁴ 2−x dx = 15/(16 ln 2). (2 marks)

(c) Use parts (a) and (b) to show that e15 < 232. (2 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) The rectangles have width 1 and heights 2⁰, 2⁻¹, 2⁻², … so their areas are 1, ½, ¼, …

This is a geometric series with a = 1 and r = ½, and |r| < 1, so
S∞ = a/(1 − r) = 1/(1 − ½) = 2, as required.

(b) ∫ 2⁻ˣ dx = −2⁻ˣ/ln 2, so
∫₀⁴ 2⁻ˣ dx = [−2⁻ˣ/ln 2]₀⁴
= (−2⁻⁴ + 2⁰)/ln 2
= (1 − 1/16)/ln 2
= 15/(16 ln 2), as required.

(c) The first four rectangles cover 0 ≤ x ≤ 4. Their total area is the limiting sum from (a) less the rectangles from x = 4 onwards:
1 + ½ + ¼ + ⅛ = 2 − (1/16 + 1/32 + …) = 2 − ⅛ = 15/8.

Because 2⁻ˣ is decreasing, each rectangle sits above the curve, so the rectangles overestimate the area:
15/8 > ∫₀⁴ 2⁻ˣ dx = 15/(16 ln 2).

Divide both sides by 15 and rearrange:
1/8 > 1/(16 ln 2)
16 ln 2 > 8
ln 2 > ½.

Multiply by 32:  32 ln 2 > 16 > 15,
so ln(2³²) > 15 and therefore 2³² > e¹⁵, that is e¹⁵ < 2³².

bandDescriptors.full: (a) a = 1, r = ½ and S∞ = 2. (b) The antiderivative −2⁻ˣ/ln 2 evaluated from 0 to 4 gives 15/(16 ln 2). (c) The rectangles overestimate the integral, giving 15/8 > 15/(16 ln 2), hence ln 2 > ½ and e¹⁵ < 2³².
bandDescriptors.partial: Parts (a) and (b) shown but (c) does not compare the correct four-rectangle sum 15/8 with the integral, or the inequality is reversed when dividing.
bandDescriptors.minimal: The rectangle areas form a geometric series with r = ½. For (b), the antiderivative of aˣ is aˣ/ln a. For (c), note the rectangles lie above the decreasing curve, so their total area exceeds the integral over the same interval.

writtenQuestions.q:
A continuous random variable X has cumulative distribution function given by
{1,   x > e³
(1/k) ln x,   1 ≤ x ≤ e³
0,   x < 1


(a) Show that k = 3. (1 mark)

(b) Given that P(X < c) = 2P(X > c), find the exact value of c. (2 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) A cumulative distribution function must reach 1 at the top of its range, and F must be continuous there.

At x = e³:  F(e³) = (1/k) ln(e³) = 3/k.
Setting 3/k = 1 gives k = 3, as required.

(b) With k = 3, F(x) = (1/3) ln x for 1 ≤ x ≤ e³.

P(X < c) = F(c) and P(X > c) = 1 − F(c), so
F(c) = 2[1 − F(c)]
3F(c) = 2
F(c) = 2/3.

Hence (1/3) ln c = 2/3, so ln c = 2 and
c = e².

(This lies in the range, since 1 ≤ e² ≤ e³.)

bandDescriptors.full: k = 3 from F(e³) = 1, and c = e² from F(c) = 2/3.
bandDescriptors.partial: k = 3 shown but (b) sets F(c) = 2/3 incorrectly — for instance solving F(c) = 2 or splitting the probability as ⅓ and ⅔ the wrong way round.
bandDescriptors.minimal: A cumulative distribution function reaches 1 at the top of its range. In (b), P(X > c) = 1 − F(c), so the condition becomes F(c) = 2[1 − F(c)].

writtenQuestions.q:
A line passes through the point P(1, 2) and meets the axes at X(x, 0) and Y(0, y), where x > 1.(a) Show that y = 2x/(x − 1). (2 marks)

(b) Find the minimum value of the area of triangle XOY. (4 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) X, P and Y are collinear, so the gradient from Y to P equals the gradient from P to X.

Gradient YP = (2 − y)/(1 − 0) = 2 − y
Gradient PX = (0 − 2)/(x − 1) = −2/(x − 1)

Set them equal:
2 − y = −2/(x − 1)
y = 2 + 2/(x − 1)
= [2(x − 1) + 2]/(x − 1)
= 2x/(x − 1), as required.

(b) Triangle XOY is right-angled at the origin with legs x and y, so
A = ½xy = ½ × x × 2x/(x − 1) = x²/(x − 1).

Differentiate with the quotient rule:
dA/dx = [2x(x − 1) − x²]/(x − 1)²
= (x² − 2x)/(x − 1)²
= x(x − 2)/(x − 1)².

dA/dx = 0 for x > 1 gives x = 2.

For 1 < x < 2, dA/dx < 0; for x > 2, dA/dx > 0. So x = 2 gives a minimum.

Minimum area = 2²/(2 − 1) = 4 square units.

bandDescriptors.full: (a) y = 2x/(x − 1) from equal gradients through P. (b) A = x²/(x − 1), dA/dx = x(x − 2)/(x − 1)², minimum at x = 2 giving area 4 square units.
bandDescriptors.partial: The area function is set up and differentiated but x = 0 is kept as a solution (it is outside x > 1), or the minimum is not verified.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Use the fact that X, P and Y lie on one line to link x and y. Then the triangle's area is ½xy — write it in terms of x alone and minimise it for x > 1.

writtenQuestions.q:
In a reducing-balance loan, an amount $P is borrowed for a period of n months at an interest rate of 0.25% per month, compounded monthly. At the end of each month, a repayment of $M is made. After the nth repayment has been made, the amount owing, $An, is given by

An = P(1.0025)n − M(1 + (1.0025)¹ + (1.0025)² + … + (1.0025)n−1).

(Do NOT prove this.)

(a) Jane borrows $200 000 in a reducing-balance loan as described.

The loan is to be repaid in 180 monthly repayments.

Show that M = 1381.16, when rounded to the nearest cent. (2 marks)

(b) After 100 repayments of $1381.16 have been made, the interest rate changes to 0.35% per month.

At this stage, the amount owing to the nearest dollar is $100 032. (Do NOT prove this.)

Jane continues to make the same monthly repayments.

For how many more months will Jane need to make full monthly payments of $1381.16? (3 marks)

(c) The final repayment will be less than $1381.16.

How much will Jane need to pay in the final payment in order to pay off the loan? (2 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) The bracket is a geometric series with a = 1, r = 1.0025 and 180 terms, so it sums to (1.0025¹⁸⁰ − 1)/0.0025.

The loan is repaid when A₁₈₀ = 0:
200 000(1.0025)¹⁸⁰ = M(1.0025¹⁸⁰ − 1)/0.0025

1.0025¹⁸⁰ ≈ 1.5674336, so
M = 200 000 × 0.0025 × 1.5674336 ÷ 0.5674336
= 783.7168 ÷ 0.5674336
≈ 1381.1633

M = $1381.16 when rounded to the nearest cent.

(b) Restart with P = 100 032, r = 0.0035 and M = 1381.16. Let x = 1.0035ⁿ.

A_n = 100 032x − 1381.16(x − 1)/0.0035 = 0
100 032x = 394 617.14(x − 1)
394 617.14 = 294 585.14x
x = 1.339569

n = ln(1.339569) ÷ ln(1.0035) ≈ 0.292348 ÷ 0.0034939 ≈ 83.67.

So after 83 more full repayments there is still a small amount owing, and the 84th payment is smaller than a full one.

Jane needs to make 83 more full monthly payments of $1381.16.

(c) Amount owing after those 83 repayments:
A₈₃ = 100 032(1.0035)⁸³ − 1381.16 × [(1.0035)⁸³ − 1]/0.0035
≈ 133 679.6 − 132 751.3
≈ $928.29

One more month's interest is charged before the final payment:
Final payment = 928.29 × 1.0035 ≈ $931.54.

bandDescriptors.full: (a) M = $1381.16 from A₁₈₀ = 0. (b) n ≈ 83.67, so 83 more full repayments. (c) A₈₃ ≈ $928.29 and the final payment is about $931.54.
bandDescriptors.partial: Parts (a) and (b) correct but the answer to (b) is rounded up to 84, or (c) gives the balance $928.29 without adding the final month's interest.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Sum the bracket as a geometric series, then set A_n = 0 to find M. In (b), restart the same formula with the new rate, the new balance and the same repayment, and solve for n — then read the non-integer answer carefully: a partial month is not a full payment.
